unmapped_findings: For the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al alloy (an intermediate Al variant), the applied aging treatments have only a weak effect on mechanical data compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening) [b0024].

In the RAP screening, intermediate alloy variants with 2–6 wt.% Al (including this 4Al sample) do not show equivalent mechanical properties to the ~8 wt.% Al variant and show a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior [b0025].

In Fig. 4, the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al (blue) points form a low-strength cluster at roughly 460–600 MPa tensile strength with elongation to fracture spanning ~8% to ~55%, aggregating multiple aging conditions (450/500/550/600 °C, 1 h and 24 h); the specific 450 °C/24 h point is not individually identified [figure_004].

Fig. 3 (RAP mechanical-property overview) plots aging curves for 450 °C/1 h, 500 °C/1 h, 550 °C/1 h, 550 °C/24 h, 600 °C/1 h, 600 °C/24 h and as-homogenised, but does not include a 450 °C/24 h curve; therefore no sample-specific YS/UTS/TE/hardness values for the 450 °C/24 h condition are individually reported in the text [figure_003].
